lens: PartForge: engineering checks the evaluation asked for
title: Torque Receipt
tagline: What a torque wrench actually promises: preload with NASA's ±25/35 % scatter from PartForge's own tables, bolt stress at the joint load against proof, and the two-pitch protrusion rule nobody checks.
pitch: Pick a size and grade, type the torque, say whether the threads were lubricated, and give the external load per bolt. The tool reads the stress area and proof load from fasteners_metric.json, the nut factor range from its design_rules, and the ±25 % / ±35 % preload uncertainty from design_factors_nasa.json, then prints F_i = T/(K·d), the min/max preload band, the bolt stress at F_i,max plus the joint load against proof and yield (no joint-stiffness credit, stated as conservative), and whether the nominal preload sits in the 0.65–0.75 proof target. A second line checks protrusion: screw length minus stack, washer and nut height against two pitches, the rule the NASA table itself says 'PartForge does not check yet'. Every verdict is COMPUTED, never PASS, because a torque-derived preload is not evidence. Run on the shipped end-cap fixture it reports that the fixture's own mfg note ('Torque M8 bolts to 25 N·m (grade 8.8 lubricated)') over-torques the bolt past proof at the high end of the scatter.
whyNow: docs/roadmap-evaluation.md ranking row idea 4 ('build trimmed (2 d of 9) — tension only: the missing tension primitive is real'); appendix #4 (worked counter-example: 25 N·m lubricated M8 8.8 → proof SF 0.82); data/tables/design_factors_nasa.json rows preload_uncertainty_lubricated (0.25), preload_uncertainty_as_received (0.35), fastener_protrusion_min ('Directly checkable … PartForge does not check it yet'), and reconciliation.withheld naming TM-106943 as the source for a preload check; data/tables/fasteners_metric.json design_rules.preload_and_torque and the torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm column; tests/dryrun/endcap.scad mfg note on 25 N·m and its 48,641 N axial load declared as bolt_shear; tests/templates/bulkhead.scad line 11 (tension declared as shear).
computes: Inputs: size (M2–M20 from fasteners_metric; UN sizes from fasteners_un with proof declared by the user because that table has no proof column — otherwise refused), grade → proof/yield/UTS from fasteners_metric.grades, T (N·m), K (0.20 dry / 0.14–0.16 lubricated from design_rules, or user with source), lubricated flag → uncertainty row, F_ext per bolt with provenance, screw length, stack thickness, washer flag. Math: F_i = T/(K·d); F_i,min/max = F_i·(1∓u); σ_max = (F_i,max + F_ext)/At vs proof and yield; target band 0.65–0.75·proof; protrusion = L_screw − (stack + washer_t + nut_h) vs 2·pitch; strip via the extracted threadCheck(). Outputs: preload band, stresses, SFs labelled COMPUTED, protrusion verdict, refusals ('tightened by feel' = no torque → refused). Measurable on the mesh: stack thickness (plate critical extent) and the clearance hole; torque, K, length and F_ext are not.
dataNeeded: snapshot.mjs copies of data/tables/fasteners_metric.json (58 KB, whole: rows, grades, design_rules) and data/tables/design_factors_nasa.json (17.8 KB); a fasteners_un.json excerpt (#2-56, #4-40, #8-32, 1/4-20 rows) by the idea's own script with --sidecar-only (~15 KB); threadCheck()/parseThreadSize() extracted from the ENG block (~5 KB); tests/dryrun/endcap.scad and tests/templates/bulkhead.scad (~25 KB). Total ≈ 120 KB.
existingOverlap: boltShear() (shear and bearing) and threadCheck() (strip) exist; dbDesignFactors() (index.html:5154) returns the preload rows and dbHints prints 'PartForge does NOT check preload, joint separation or joint slip' (:5502). No tension primitive and no protrusion check exist. The evaluation warns an inline proof table would duplicate fasteners_metric.json; this tool consumes that table's proof_load_* and torque_guide columns instead. Joint separation is deliberately not built (both skeptics: separation is the wrong criterion for a radial piston seal).
honestyRisks: Proof vs yield vs UTS confusion inflates SF 10–40 % — the fields are named and printed separately. Torque is not evidence (fasteners_metric: 'do not rely on torque alone for a pressure boundary') so every row is COMPUTED. K is a design-rule range, not a measurement, and the row says which value was used. No joint diagram, so bolt stress at F_i,max + F_ext is conservative and labelled so. UN proof strengths are absent from the repo and are refused unless declared with a source. Finding to report: the end-cap fixture's 25 N·m lubricated M8 8.8 note gives F_i 20.8 kN against a 21.2 kN proof load, 712 MPa at +25 %.
testPlan: torque.test.mjs: for all 12 metric sizes, torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm/(0.2·d)/proof_load_8_8_N lands in [0.697, 0.702] (reconciling the table's own column to K 0.2 and 70 % proof, as its design rule states); the evaluation's counter-example M8 8.8, 25 N·m, K 0.15 → F_i 20,833 N vs proof 21,200 N; at 1.25× → 711.5 MPa → proof SF 0.82; M6 at 9 mm engagement reproduces the repo's threadCheck test vector (tests/flight-eng.test.mjs:246); protrusion: a 20 mm M6 through 10 mm plate + 1.6 washer + 5.2 nut → 3.2 mm ≥ 2.0 passes, a 16 mm screw fails; refusals for no torque, UN size without declared proof, unknown grade. Browser smoke at 390 px.
landing: index.html: a bolt_tension loads kind in the ENG block and evaluator, a protrusion rule in flightLint (~:4855), and a partTier() note so a pressure part with only tension rows does not stay tier A (evaluation hook note); the doctrine line 'does NOT check preload' changes; headless rebuild. To ship, read fasteners_metric through dbRows('fasteners_metric') rather than this snapshot; TM-106943 is the named source to validate against.
notes: Verified fasteners_metric grades/design_rules and design_factors_nasa preload_uncertainty rows; endcap.scad notes 25 N·m lubricated M8 8.8 and a protrusion rule 'PartForge does not check yet'. Tension primitive the ranking says is real.

Verified GRADE_SY at :5804 now has grade 2 = 393, endcap.scad:51 says torque M8 to 25 N·m lubricated, and design_factors rows preload_uncertainty_*/fastener_protrusion_min exist; the over-proof finding follows from table fields.

fasteners_metric.json has proof_load_* and torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm columns and design_factors_nasa has the preload_uncertainty and fastener_protrusion_min rows, so the tool is buildable. But the pitched finding is misattributed: tests/dryrun/endcap.scad contains no 'Torque M8 bolts to 25 N·m (lubricated)' note; that worked example is the roadmap appendix's (line 403), and the fixture's own line 11 computes 6,080 N per bolt.
